validation.0.1.5-alpha.1: 58 automated tests, real Cordis Loader/Connection activation with dynamic trustedHosts interpolation, and RPC authentication/disposal checks. User confirmed successful DSH startup with the corrected webRuntime/webServer dependency list; no live model or full account-flow verification.
validation.0.1.5-alpha.2: Offline tests against the published host packages cover resolution and call preparation of every advertised Kimi model using the real PiAiAdapter, Cordis Loader/Connection activation and RPC authentication/disposal, and the actual adapter retry policy through the real retry executor and Session event validation (six retryable codes, finite backoff, two-retry limit, original failure preservation, provider-directed delays, and cancellation). No live model calls, real credential reads, or full GUI/account-flow verification.
validation.0.1.7-rc.1: Offline tests run against the published 0.1.7-rc.1 host packages, the same version as the desktop app. They cover the desktop installer's peer-range gate, activation without the removed settings.register API, model resolution and call preparation through the real PiAiAdapter, Cordis Loader/Connection activation (including the legacy 0.1.2-alpha.5 Connection), RPC authentication/disposal, and the adapter retry policy. A scratch profile boot confirms the account route mounts. No live model calls, real credential reads, or desktop GUI verification.
validation.0.1.7-rc.2: The desktop app auto-updated to this release. Its app-boot compatibility gate accepts the declared peer range, the client modules this plugin injects are all present, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` still export `LlmError`, `resolveRetryPolicy`, and `PiAiAdapter`. The settings service still has no `register`, so the volatile-Config path is the one that runs. A scratch profile boot on this kernel activates the account route. The device authorization request was also exercised against the live Kimi endpoint; the token exchange is covered by offline tests only, including the compressed-body and classified-failure paths. Release 1.3.1 additionally exercised the plugin self-update path against this exact desktop runtime with the shipped bundle: the live host process's own launch arguments were replayed, the bundled pnpm 11.7.0 entry was selected by name, and `update()` installed the target version into a scratch desktop profile and rewrote its dependency while keeping the `dsh.profile.bundles` entry. That run also confirmed `dsh plugin --profile desktop` is refused by this CLI, which is why the update installs with pnpm directly. No live model calls or credential reads.
validation.0.2.0-rc.2: DeepSeek Harness.app 0.2.0-rc.2 and its bundled CLI are the same host line. `dsh web --dump-default-config` on that CLI shows the official connection row injects only webRuntime; the string webServer does not appear anywhere in the default tree. Desktop loads the same @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app@0.2.0-rc.2 bundle, so deleting the connection patch would drop webServer on both surfaces. A scratch web profile with this plugin linked composes inject [credentials, webRuntime, webServer], keeps trustedHosts as the webRuntime expression, and reaches the listen line with no 'did not activate' warning. The offline suite still runs on the 0.2.0-rc.1 packages already in the lockfile; connection's published 0.2.0-rc.2 bundle is byte-identical to 0.2.0-rc.1. No live model calls, credential reads, or desktop GUI verification.
validation.0.2.0-rc.1: The desktop app updated to this release. Its app-boot compatibility preflight had disabled the whole bundle, because every declared `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer stopped at `<0.2.0-0`; the profile startup line was `skipping profile bundle "dsh-kimi-subscription": Error: Plugin dsh-kimi-subscription@1.3.1 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.1`. That denial was reproduced against a scratch profile on the real desktop runtime, and the widened range was confirmed to clear it. Every host package this plugin consumes is present at 0.2.0-rc.1, every module named in `dsh.client.inject` resolves, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` still exports `LlmError` and `resolveRetryPolicy`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai` still exports `PiAiAdapter`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` still has no `register`, so the volatile-Config path is the one that runs. The development baseline and the whole offline suite now run against the published 0.2.0-rc.1 host packages and pi-ai 0.87.1, which the 0.2 line resolves through `^0.85.1`; `kimiCodingProvider` is unchanged between pi-ai 0.85.1 and 0.87.1. No live model calls, credential reads, or desktop GUI verification.
validation.0.2.1-rc.1: DeepSeek Harness.app 0.2.1-rc.1 renamed the service the official connection row injects from webRuntime to webStartup (trustedHosts: !!js ctx.webStartup.trustedHosts). With 1.3.8 installed the desktop app did not boot: the bundle's row patch replaced that inject list with [credentials, webRuntime, webServer], and the host listed `connection (required)  webRuntime` among the plugins waiting for services. `--dump-config` on the app's bundled CLI, run against a scratch DSH_HOME, composes exactly that row for 1.3.8 and leaves the official [webStartup] row untouched for 1.3.9; the bundle passes the app-boot peer gate in both. The whole offline suite also runs against the host packages extracted from that app (cordis 4.0.5, cordis-plugin-loader 1.0.6, cordis-plugin-include 1.0.10, dsh-client-connection, dsh-llm, and dsh-llm-pi-ai 0.2.1-rc.1, pi-ai 1.1.0) through a resolver hook with no fallback to the development baseline: all 106 tests pass, including activation on the official 0.2.1 row, a web server that starts after the plugin, and rejection of unauthenticated requests. Cordis 4.0.5's runtime is byte-identical to 4.0.4, and pi-ai 1.1.0's kimiCodingProvider is unchanged. This host's adapter lists a provider's models only after resolveApiKey succeeds, so an unconnected subscription shows no Kimi models. The published 0.2.1-rc.1 packages are younger than the release-age window, so the development baseline stays at 0.2.0-rc.1. Desktop was not restarted. No live model calls, credential reads, or desktop GUI verification.
validation.0.2.1-rc.3: The development baseline moved to the host packages DeepSeek Harness.app 0.2.1-rc.3 ships: dsh 0.2.1-rc.3, cordis 4.0.5, cordis-plugin-loader 1.0.6, cordis-plugin-include 1.0.10, schemastery 3.18.5, and pi-ai 1.1.0, read from the app bundle. As in the app, the llm-pi-ai adapter and the plugin now load one pi-ai copy, and a contract test keeps them on it. The previous baseline paired the 0.2.0-rc.1 adapter, which depends on pi-ai ^0.85.1, with the plugin on 0.87.1. pi-ai 0.87.1 expects the system prompt and tools folded into the transcript and 0.85.1 hands them over unfolded, so every Kimi request lost both without an error. A desktop profile whose installed plugin still carried a node_modules copied from a local-path install ran that same pairing, and Kimi ended every turn after one reply without calling a tool. All offline tests pass on the new baseline, including a request through the real adapter that must carry the system prompt and tools. dsh-invariants left the baseline: no 0.2.1 package depends on it and the app does not ship it. After that copy was removed and the user restarted the app, the next session in DeepSeek Harness.app 0.2.1-rc.3 had k3.1-pro-highspeed call bash, glob, grep, and read 15 times. This change made no live model calls and read no credentials.
validation.0.2.1-rc.5: The test suite now also runs against the host packages DeepSeek Harness.app 0.2.1-rc.5 ships, read from its app.asar: dsh 0.2.1-rc.5, cordis 4.0.5, cordis-plugin-loader 1.0.6, cordis-plugin-include 1.0.10, schemastery 3.18.5, and pi-ai 1.1.0. They are installed in tests/hosts/dsh-0.2.1, and `pnpm run test:dsh-0.2.1` resolves every host import from there through a resolver hook, with no fallback to the root's 0.2.2 packages. All offline tests pass on it. Kimi requests still use Anthropic Messages at /coding/v1/messages. On this host the account channel used to open only because the plugin wrote webServer onto Connection's fiber, which also restarted Connection whenever the web server restarted; a test now requires Connection to stay up. No live model calls, credential reads, or desktop GUI verification.
validation.0.2.2-rc.1: DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 ships cordis 4.1.0 and pi-ai 1.3.0, read from the dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1 lockfile of deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness; its pi-ai patch only drops streaming tool-argument parsing and adds a Gemini signature. Two failures on this host are fixed. Cordis 4.1.0 resolves services through fiber.committed and fiber.provisions, so the plugin's write to Connection's fiber had no effect and the account channel never opened: /kimi-subscription answered 405 (issue #7). The plugin now passes its own web context to Connection's channel registration. pi-ai 1.3.0 speaks OpenAI Chat Completions to Kimi Code under /coding/v1, while the plugin's region table fixed /coding, so every model request went to /coding/chat/completions, which both Kimi sites answer with 404 (probed without credentials; /coding/v1/chat/completions answers 401). Each region now keeps the catalog's path on its own API host. The development baseline moved to these packages: dsh 0.2.2-rc.1, cordis 4.1.0, cordis-plugin-loader 1.1.0, cordis-plugin-include 1.1.0, schemastery 3.19.0, and pi-ai 1.3.0 without the upstream patch. All offline tests pass on it, including a signed-in HTTP request through the account channel and a request through the real adapter that must carry the system prompt and tools. pi-ai 1.3.0 lists the same four Kimi Code IDs; with no effort chosen a request sends no thinking field, and a chosen effort is sent as reasoning_effort. Not verified: a live model call, multi-turn tool use, whether Kimi accepts reasoning_effort max, and the plan-rejection message of the Chat Completions endpoint. The desktop app was not run on this version.
